en: The Sūtra on the Wheel of Dedication Spoken by the Buddha, in one fascicle.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīladharma of Khotan at Longxing Monastery in Beiting.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was dwelling upon the peak of the Great Maṇi Vajra Jewel Mountain.
Together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas,
the World-Honored One then addressed the Bodhisattva Vajramaṇi, saying:
"O Son of the Buddha, if there is a bodhisattva who seeks great enlightenment..."
Desiring to rescue and deliver all sentient beings,
they have already received the bodhisattva vows and precepts,
and having completed their studies, they have already generated the mind of great enlightenment.
Possessing great compassion,
he constantly desires to serve all Tathāgatas and wishes to extensively accumulate the stores of merit and wisdom of the great Bodhisattvas.
Desiring to realize the wisdom of a Buddha;
desiring to sport with the unimpeded samādhis, dhāraṇīs, all doors of liberation, and supernormal powers;
desiring to transform empty space into a great treasury.
Wishing to cause my own hands to resemble wish-fulfilling jewels so as to make this offering,
I pray that all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones,
and the great Bodhisattvas who have already dwelled in the ten stages [will accept it].
O Vajradhara, please keep me in mind. I,
the disciple [Name], have already generated the bodhicitta but have not yet become established in the right path.
Now, with my body and mind,
at all times and in every way,
I offer them as a gift to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time.
May the Great Sovereign Buddhas, Tathāgatas,
and all Bodhisattvas who have realized the great stages,
please accept me.
May my great provisions of merit and wisdom,
my fierce and sharp diligence, my vast mental capacity,
and my tranquil self-mastery through the supernormal powers be perfected.
The pāramitās will be swiftly brought to fulfillment.
Furthermore, he spoke these words:
"O Great Compassionate One, please take me into your mindful care."
I, disciple [Name], have fallen into the cycle of birth and death, bound by great fetters,
confined within a prison, separated from the Dharma of the True Path,
and coerced by the powerful enemies of the afflictions.
Without protection, without rescue, without eyes, and without reliance;
without a leader and without a guide, they wander upon deviant paths,
heading toward birth and death while turning their backs on Great Nirvana.
They follow toward the various evil destinies and are about to fall onto perilous paths;
on the verge of collapsing into the miserable realms, they constantly encounter evil companions,
while being separated from virtuous friends and becoming confused regarding what is heterodox and what is orthodox.
They pursue profit and abandon what is beneficial; they pursue the meaningless and abandon what is meaningful.
They distance themselves from all that is wholesome and accomplish what is unwholesome.
They constantly turn their backs on the worthy and noble ones, the Buddhas, and the Bodhisattvas.
Oppressed by birth, old age, sickness, death,
and affliction, they find no peace, security, fearlessness, or intrepidity;
their minds are constantly distracted, and they lack the cultivation of tranquility, self-discipline, generosity, ethical conduct, and heedfulness.
They are far removed from the two gates of meditative concentration (*samādhi*) and dhāraṇī, the ten stages (*bhūmi*), and the patient acceptance of dharmas (*dharmakṣānti*);
they are unable to abide in profound *prajñāpāramitā* and in equanimity (*samatā*).
They do not cultivate the immeasurable states of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity;
they are not endowed with the bodhisattva’s threefold aggregate of ethical discipline;
and they remain far removed from unobstructed and unhindered great wisdom.
They are unable to abide securely in the well-established dharmas that are the causes of tranquility;
they are devoid of the powers of supernormal knowledge and the fearlessnesses;
they do not dwell in right mindfulness, and they cannot achieve the dharma of non-forgetfulness that follows and enters into practice.
Lacking all meritorious qualities,
they are hindered by views and doubt from attaining the seven factors of enlightenment,
and they fail to cultivate the eightfold noble path as it truly is.
Oppressed by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of afflictions,
they are constantly ablaze and beset by manifold sufferings;
their minds are perpetually base, full of resentment, and distracted.
Constantly following after afflictions,
I only pray that all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
relying on their great compassion and pity, will provide me with protection and refuge.
Be my refuge and my guide.
I pray that you may cause me to swiftly attain the path of great, perfect enlightenment—
the way of great bodhi and the provisions for awakening.
Furthermore, I pray that I may swiftly attain the perfection of the Tathāgata’s ten powers, the four fearlessnesses,
the eighteen unique qualities of a Tathāgata,
unimpeded eloquence, meditative concentrations, liberations, and dhāraṇī-gates.
The perfection of merit and supernormal powers.
Furthermore, may all accomplishments and all merits be granted to me.
Next, when performing extensive offerings, one should speak as follows:
Furthermore, I pray that all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones,
and the assembly of Bodhisattvas who have already attained great power,
will keep me in their mindful recollection.
I, the disciple [Name],
now before all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, turn toward them with great reverence,
serving and making offerings, and dedicate my very body as an offering.
All the great ornaments of adornment within all the worlds of the ten directions—
namely, various jeweled palaces,
jewel-adorned trees, and jewel mountains.
Jeweled thrones and jeweled altars arranged in rows of precious gems;
jeweled canopies, jeweled banners, and jeweled ornaments and necklaces;
nets of pearls, jeweled vessels, heaps of jewels, and the blazing radiance of jewels.
Upon those various jewel islands, great maṇi jewels and pure lamp-trees resound with the harmonious chiming of precious bells;
the radiance of the maṇis shines forth like tassels of pure gold.
Overhanging and interconnected are exquisite golden lotuses,
with filaments made of Jāmbūnada gold;
rows of golden trees stand amidst various jeweled palaces.
Jewel clouds gathered and rained down droplets of various jewels;
within the halls of the jewel treasuries were exquisite maṇi gems,
interspersed among the walls and railings of precious beads.
The great vidyādhara delights in a perfect garden;
his dwellings, precious palaces, halls, and groves are all delightful.
Yet, these things are without grasping and without appropriation.
Dedicate this to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
May all the excellent medicines and longevity-inducing substances found in Jambudvīpa,
as well as all maṇi-jewels, grant sentient beings whatever medicinal remedies they seek.
Naturally produced exquisite and superior foods and drinks,
as well as various kinds of fragrant trees,
such as sandalwood trees and agalloch trees.
There are species of trees such as agallochum, red sandalwood,
mahāpatra, nityapuṣpa, and those with intoxicating fragrances;
there are also delightful, wondrously scented *kalpavṛkṣa* trees that are neither grasped nor appropriated.
Within the great ocean, there are various kinds of diverse mani-jewels, wish-fulfilling gems,
as well as Mount Sumeru and Mount Kīṣa-ra.
Mount Gandhamādana, Mount Maṇijaya,
the great mountain Indraya,
Mount Mandara, Mount Vajra, and so forth.
Within the various great mountains, there are peaks of diverse jewels,
jeweled terraces, precious stones, jeweled caves, and jeweled palaces;
there are jewel ornaments, fragments of gems, and stairways made of many kinds of jewels.
The various mani-pillars and various jeweled lamp-circles;
all the celestial palaces of the lordless devas, consisting of varieties of mani-gems such as lapis lazuli and the like.
The various celestial flowers are pleasing and delightful to behold;
the various celestial musical instruments are stirred by a gentle breeze;
and the rows of celestial palaces in the sky resonate with harmonious and beautiful sounds.
The various celestial musical instruments produced exquisite sounds spontaneously without being struck.
The various birds of the heavens, dwelling within their palaces in the sky,
emitted wondrous cries, while the various jewel-clouds likewise produced magnificent sounds.
There were celestial mani-jewels, songs, and instrumental music,
as well as trees of exquisite fragrant flowers, garlands, ointments, and incense,
along with trees of lamps, banners, pennants, and precious gems.
All these are without anything to be grasped;
they are offered as gifts to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas—
everything that is perceived by the Buddha-eye.
Great clouds of offerings within the buddha-fields:
clouds of flowers, clouds of incense, clouds of garlands, clouds of burning incense,
clouds of ointment, clouds of precious parasols, clouds of precious banners, and clouds of precious pennants.
Clouds of precious robes, clouds of gathered jewels, clouds of precious vessels, and clouds of great masses of mani-jewels;
as well as clouds of various kinds of exquisite and wondrous great precious pearls;
furthermore, large lamp-vessels filled with fragrant oil.
With lamp-wicks equal in size to a thousand world-systems and as large as a hundred Sumeru mountains,
one offers them to all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, and the great Bodhisattvas.
May the supreme merit arising from these offerings be dedicated toward unsurpassed enlightenment,
just as all the virtues cultivated by the Buddhas of the past.
Using non-apprehension as the skillful means,
I dedicate this toward enlightenment;
I likewise maintain these merits in this same manner.
Dedicate [the merit] toward unexcelled,
perfect enlightenment and entreat all Buddhas,
praying only that they proceed to the site of enlightenment.
Having subdued the hosts of Māra and realized great Bodhi, he turned the Great Wheel of Dharma;
now, for the sake of all sentient beings who desire his parinirvāṇa,
we entreat him to remain for the full duration of one great kalpa.
I rejoice in all the merits cultivated by all Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and all sentient beings.
I confess and repent for all my transgressions,
just as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the three periods of time have confessed their karmic obscurations.
I likewise vow that my transgressions shall be extinguished.
Having completed the offerings and the confession,
I shall immediately, with a pure mind, bring to mind all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
Before the image of the Buddha, recite this mantra eight times until it is complete.
The mantra is: Oṃ sphara sphara vimanasvara mahājvāla hūṃ. Having recited the mantra, [proceed].
Even as they wish,
they shall accomplish vast clouds of sublime celestial offerings that appear before all Buddhas.
If a son of good family or a daughter of good family,
with mindfulness fixed upon the Buddha, whether by day or by night,
recites and turns this Great Wheel of Dedication.
These good sons or good daughters shall have all their transgressions extinguished and all afflictions gradually become thin and slight;
they will be able to attain the merits previously described.
If one recites it once, one will obtain a hundred merits of Brahmā;
one will constantly see the Buddha in dreams;
and after the end of life, one will attain rebirth in a Pure Land.
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the assembly of bodhisattvas rejoiced and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra on the Wheel of Dedication Spoken by the Buddha.
